extracted.intended_audience: academics and practitioners in fashion communication, public relations, and brand/crisis managers
extracted.subtask_description: A scholarly case-study focused on analyzing a major fashion brand's crisis communication (Balenciaga) on social media, extracting lessons about response strategy, reputation effects, and measurement. Useful for researchers and PR/brand practitioners developing crisis-response policies for fashion/luxury brands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis definition and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: A crisis is “a low probability, high impact event that threatens the viability of the organization and is characterized by ambiguity of cause, effect and means of resolution, as well as by a belief that decisions must be made quickly.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition to determine when a situation requires crisis-mode responses (urgency, cross-functional decision-making). Recognize ambiguity of cause/effect and that rapid decisions will be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis management objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Crisis management follows two fundamental objectives: firstly stopping adverse trends and handling the crisis situation (survival), and secondly reaching a turning point (redirectioning) and ensuring the foundations for new development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan immediate containment actions and a parallel strategy for organizational learning and repositioning post-crisis; measure success both by mitigation and by steps toward recovery/redirection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of crisis types
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitroff and Pearson identify seven groups of major crisis events: economic attacks, environmental accidents, occupational health diseases, psycho events (e.g., terrorism, sabotage, product tampering), damage to reputation, informational attacks, and breaks (e.g., recalls, product defects, computer breakdowns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify the event to tailor response tactics; reputation-related crises (most common in fashion) require particular PR and stakeholder strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting reputation as a strategic asset
rubrics_metrics.description: Reputation is how an organization is perceived by its public and is a crucial resource worthy of protection and concern during a crisis; brands with favorable reputations have more loyal customers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize actions that limit reputational damage (transparent communication, accountability) because reputation loss can have long-term business impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of response
rubrics_metrics.description: Slow, unclear and unaccountable answers compose a terrible strategy of crisis management; Balenciaga’s slow response (7 days to full apology) exacerbated the crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond quickly and clearly. Delays allow virality and media amplification; set internal SLAs for initial public response and follow-ups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and accountability in messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: The brand’s initial strategy to portray itself as a victim and place full blame on the production company kindled consumer anger; an eventual apology that takes responsibility is the most convincing option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt clear, accountable messages; avoid deflective scapegoating. If at fault, employ apology/deal response options promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of response strategy (deny vs deal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Response options include 'Deny Response Option' (scapegoat/blame outside parties) and 'Deal Response Option' (apology/taking full responsibility); the latter is more convincing if adopted timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether denial/scapegoating will be perceived as evasive; prefer sincere responsibility-taking when evidence suggests internal accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding defensive legal gestures that appear evasive
rubrics_metrics.description: Balenciaga filed a $25 million lawsuit against production partners as part of a deflective strategy; this action was perceived as attempt to shift blame and aggravated public suspicion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider reputational impact before initiating high-profile legal actions; weigh short-term legal strategy against potential public perception of evasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform-specific strategy and audience awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Different social platforms have different formats and demographics (e.g., TikTok is fast-growing, audiovisual, targets Gen Z); crises can originate and spread differently by platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor monitoring and response per platform; prioritize channels where target audiences engage (e.g., TikTok for Gen Z). Do not treat all platforms identically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and measuring social media impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative metrics such as likes, comments, shares, views and engagement levels (measured via tools like Fanpage Karma) quantify the magnitude and virality of crises (e.g., hashtag views, follower losses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use social analytics tools to track hashtag views, engagement, follower changes, and timeline trends; report both absolute and relative changes to evaluate severity and recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listening and two-way communication
rubrics_metrics.description: User generated content and two-way communication are central to Web 2.0; brands should listen and interact rather than mute or remain silent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid freezing accounts or muting comments for extended periods; use social listening to surface concerns, correct misinformation, and demonstrate engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate consumer empowerment and value-alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumers are empowered on social media to demand, praise and cancel; social causes are often aligned with shared moral and ethical values (e.g., child protection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether campaign content may violate widely held social norms; conduct stakeholder/value alignment checks prior to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional dynamics of virality (anger as a driver)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anger is the most viral emotion on the Internet and can lead to boycotts if the crisis is not managed efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft communications that acknowledge and address emotional concerns; recognize that anger-driven content spreads rapidly and requires fast mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content validation and governance controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Balenciaga announced actions such as new control instances for content validation and a reorganization of their image department as remedies after the crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement pre-publication content review, governance processes, and sign-offs to prevent inappropriate imagery or references; define escalation paths for sensitive content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and actor-analysis in post-crisis evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze the timeline of events, the actors involved, and the communication strategies taken during the scandal to understand failures and consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use qualitative timeline mapping plus quantitative metrics to reconstruct event propagation and identify decision points that worsened or mitigated the crisis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Celebrity/influencer risk and relationship management
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrity statements (e.g., Kim Kardashian) and influencer actions (removing posts, refusing brand ties) influence public attention and can escalate searches and reputational impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor high-profile stakeholders and maintain influencer/celebrity engagement plans; prepare contingency outreach to key ambassadors following controversies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for social ethical boundaries (sensitive content guardrails)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are social anethical boundaries (e.g., protecting child rights) that brands must not cross; linking campaigns to minors and sexualized imagery provoked public outrage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish explicit ethical guardrails and red-lines (especially regarding minors, exploitation, hate/race/sexualization) for creative concepts and marketing materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of remedial and restorative actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-crisis remedies included internal/external investigations, dropping lawsuits, reorganizing teams, and donations to child protection organizations as steps to 'learn from our mistakes'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design remediation packages combining accountability, systemic change, and community/NGO engagement to rebuild trust; communicate tangible steps and timelines.
